text.card: Set and clear fixed queens without row, column or diagonal attacks.
text.hands_empty: Put down what you hold before changing a queen indicator.
text.occupied: That fixed cell indicator is already occupied. Remove it or choose another unthreatened cell.
text.attacked: A queen already attacks this row, column or diagonal. Remove an indicator to backtrack, or choose a cell not attacked.
text.already_empty: That fixed cell indicator is already empty. Place a legal queen or remove an occupied cell.
text.coordinates: This is a four-by-four nonattacking-queens diagram. Seen from the front contact side, rows1 through4 run from the far/top edge toward you, with row numbers on the left. Columns1 through4 run left to right, numbered across the far edge. Each cell has its own original fixed base-and-crown indicator. A place form shows that indicator only if the cell and every other cell in its row, column and both diagonals are empty. A remove form hides only an occupied indicator.
text.worked_first: One complete solution has row1 column3, row2 column1, row3 column4 and row4 column2. Set these four indicators in order; no two share a row, column or diagonal. To clear the board, remove each occupied indicator. There is no reset, automatic solver, score, hatch, winner or claim state.
text.worked_second: The other complete solution has row1 column2, row2 column4, row3 column1 and row4 column3. Both solutions are listed as ordinary actions, not automatically selected. You may remove any occupied indicator at any time to backtrack.
text.backtrack: A legal but nonextendable three-queen partial position is row1 column1, row2 column4, row3 column2. No fourth queen can be added. Remove those occupied indicators to return to empty, then try a different first placement. Mistakes are expected puzzle work; a refused conflicting placement leaves the board unchanged.
text.limits: This is an indexed fixed-indicator constraint diagram with sixteen original per-cell assemblies. Occupied means that cell indicator is shown; empty hides it without creating or destroying pieces. No loose-piece custody, physical queen movement, precise individual-cell finger contact, turn enforcement, alternating multiplayer chess, captures or check rules are claimed.
